Subject: RFI: Airlock placement + connector proxies

Ava —

Thanks for taking the RFI. NorthStar's security team is reviewing Redwood's proposed topology for our regulated inference workloads and we need clarifications around three items in particular: the airlock (gateway) placement, connector/sidecar proxy behavior, and tenant-fencing guarantees. Can you provide:

- A diagram that shows the airlock gateway relative to control plane and data plane (we're interested in whether customer model payloads traverse shared control-plane subnets)
- A description of connector (sidecar) egress rules: which destinations are allowed by default and how they can be restricted (IP allowlist, FQDN, service tags)
- The failure behavior: if the sidecar loses reachability to the gateway, does inference traffic fail/queue/retry and what telemetry is captured

We've attached our standard RFI template for reference (NorthStar-RFI-Template.pdf). Please include any evidence artifacts you can (network diagrams, ACL examples, audit log retention statements).

We're on a tight timeline — security needs initial answers by EOD Tue 11/9. If you can point us to a short evidence packet and propose a follow-up call that would be helpful.

Best,
Alice Morton
Enterprise Security Program Manager
NorthStar Bank

Alice —

Thanks for the clear asks and for the template. I've attached a compact evidence packet and two diagrams to address each point: redwood-airlock-gateway-20261108.png and connector-proxy-flow-20261108.pdf (see attachments list). Also attached is an "airlock-evidence-checklist.xlsx" that maps our doc artifacts to your template headers.

High level answers (summary):
- Airlock placement: The Airlock Gateway is deployed in a tenant-bound subnet within a dedicated data-plane VPC per-customer for our Dedicated/Private customers. For Redwood-hosted (multi-tenant) customers we terminate model payloads into isolated per-tenant compute slices; control-plane traffic (orchestration calls) goes over a separate, authenticated control plane that does NOT carry model payloads. The diagram shows the demarcation and the ACLs that prevent model payload egress to control-plane services.

- Connector / Sidecar egress rules: By default sidecars are configured to allow outbound DNS + KMS endpoints + Redwood routing mesh (for model variants). Customers can switch to an explicit allowlist mode: (1) IP CIDR allowlists, (2) FQDN allowlists via egress proxy rules, or (3) private peering where only enterprise endpoints are reachable. We include examples in the attached PDF: sample egress ACLs and iptables snippets for on-prem/private deployments.

- Failure behavior & telemetry: If the sidecar loses connectivity to the Airlock Gateway the observed behavior depends on the deployment mode:
  * Private / Dedicated: requests fail with 502 and clients see deterministic error codes. We capture the failed request, KV cache state, and a full trace (request id, model variant id) in our local telemetry. Retries are application controlled — default SDK does 2 backoffs.
  * Hosted: we have a circuit-breaker that transitions traffic to a compatible degraded model variant (lower memory/quantized) if the primary path is congested; if network reachability fails outright requests fail and we log the event into the customer's audit stream.

Evidence included:
- redwood-airlock-gateway-20261108.png (logical topology)
- connector-proxy-flow-20261108.pdf (ejection and allowlist examples)
- airlock-evidence-checklist.xlsx (artifact mapping to your template)

Next steps I propose: 30 minute call to walk the diagram and confirm private peering options. I can also provide a short runbook excerpt showing audit log retention (we keep request-level metadata for 13 months by default; SOC2/attestation extracts available on request).

Availability: Mon 11/9 10:00–11:30 PST or Tue 11/10 14:00–16:00 PST. Which slot works?

Thanks — happy to expand any section.

Looping in a couple of operational details that often come up in procurement reviews — adding here so Alice has concrete examples to validate in your checklist.

- Sidecar keepalive & fail-open policy: our sidecar defaults to fail-closed for private deployments (no outbound allowed unless whitelisted). For hosted customers we provide a configurable fail-policy; however the default is not to silently fail-open.

- KV cache & replay protection: we persist minimal KV cache metadata in an encrypted store (per-tenant key). Cache items are not exfiltrated to control plane. We included a short operator-playbook-stub.txt with exemplar commands to rotate keys and scrub cache artifacts.

- Interconnect: we support private peering (VPC/VNET), customer-owned transit gateway attachments, and GRE-style tunnels for on-prem. If NorthStar requires that model payload never traverse public IPs we can propose a private-only SLA and a runbook for annual validation.

I'll be on the call on Tue if scheduled.

Ben
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Alice —

Thanks — answers inline below and next steps at the bottom.

1) Audit retention & export format:
- Retention: default 13 months; configurable up to 36 months via enterprise retention add-on. We can set per-tenant retention windows and produce export snapshots for compliance.
- Export formats: NDJSON is our standard for request-level events (timestamped JSON lines) and we also support Parquet exports for high-volume ingestion. We'll include a sample NDJSON export mapping in the compliance packet.

2) Canonical ACL snippet (deny-by-default, minimal allowlist) — sample for Linux sidecar iptables (illustrative):

# flush existing
iptables -F
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP

# allow loopback and DNS
iptables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
ip6tables -A OUTPUT -p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT

# allow KMS + telemetry + airlock gateway (replace with enterprise CIDRs)
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 10.2.0.0/24 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT  # Airlock gateway
iptable -A OUTPUT -d 10.3.5.0/28 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT  # KMS endpoints

# block everything else (implicit by policy)

Note: for hosted customers we enforce equivalent egress restrictions at the VPC egress layer if private peering is used.

3) Private-only SLA and costs:
- We can offer a private-only deployment guarantee (no public IP hops for model payloads) under Redwood Dedicated / Private contracts. This is scoped as an addendum (Private Peering SLA). It includes annual validation, network proof artifacts, and a private-only uptime SLA. Pricing: additional networking/peering engineering and reserved capacity are charged — estimated uplift typically 15–25% depending on throughput and cross-region attachments. We can provide a formal quote if NorthStar wants to proceed.

Next steps and action items:
- I'll drop a compliance packet that includes NDJSON sample, parquet export spec, and the finalized iptables examples (ETA EOD Wed 11/11).
- Proposed call: Tue 11/10 15:00 PST (30 minutes) — agenda: confirm private peering design, retention window, and finalize checklist items. Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.ai/s/ava_chen/call-20261110

If that's good, I'll have Marissa prepare the SLA addendum draft and Irene prepare SOC2 evidence extracts. Ben will join the call for infra deep-dive.

Thanks — talk soon.
